name: core-catalog-path-loses-a-segment
why: catalogFilePath() is where the engine decides whether the large-repo layer is on at all. Losing a path segment makes every catalog scenario answer as if no catalog existed, and the baseline has to see catalogPresent and every catalog-driven command move together.

name: catalog-lint-exit-code-inverted
why: catalog-lint's exit code is the contract CI and the commit hooks read: 0 means the catalog is coherent. A baseline that cannot see 0 and 1 swap cannot see a gate invert.

name: impact-exit-code-inverted
why: rc 3 means degraded and rc 0 means answered. Swapping them makes a real impact analysis read as 'could not tell' and a degraded one read as authoritative -- the exact confusion the rc 3 convention exists to prevent.

name: verify-blocked-state-not-aggregated
why: one blocked check has to block the whole run. Demanding that every check be blocked first turns 'the security scanner is not installed' into a pass, which is the failure mode BLOCKED was invented for.

name: fitness-rule-severity-raised
why: severity is what turns a fitness finding into a blocker: it drives the counts, the ok flag and the exit code. A ruler that cannot see a rule's severity move cannot tell a warning from a red gate.

name: context-pack-diff-budget-inverted
find: const entry = { path: '<canonical-diff>', bytes: Math.min(diffChars, maxDiffChars), reason: 'diff' };
replace: const entry = { path: '<canonical-diff>', bytes: Math.max(diffChars, maxDiffChars), reason: 'diff' };
why: the diff is charged min(actual, cap) against the pack budget; max() bills a two-line diff for the whole cap and crowds real files out. It also moves packHash, the digest this baseline deliberately refuses to mask.

name: gate-blocked-stops-blocking
why: gate rc 2 is what pre-commit-check reads to stop a commit. A BLOCKED run that stops producing a blocking gate is the most expensive silent regression in the engine: everything still looks like it ran.

name: task-envelope-drops-escalation
why: the envelope's required fields are the dispatch contract. A field quietly leaving the list shows up nowhere except a shorter `missing` array, which is precisely what a field-by-field baseline is for.

name: trace-min-coverage-defaults-to-zero
why: trace demands full coverage unless told otherwise. Defaulting to 0 lets any set of unverified requirements pass, and the only witnesses are the echoed minCoverage field and the exit code.

name: review-max-rounds-off-by-one
why: maxRounds decides when a repeatedly rejected change escalates instead of looping. It is echoed into every verdict, so a baseline blind to it is blind to the escalation rule moving.

name: memory-view-drops-tail-reserve
find: const room = Math.max(0, budget - header.length - TAIL_RESERVE);
why: the tail reserve is what keeps the 'N item(s) omitted' line inside the budget the caller asked for. Without it a budgeted view overruns the budget exactly when it has bad news to deliver.

name: release-worktree-always-clean
why: the worktree check is the one that says what would ship is what was tested. Always answering PASS makes the readiness report lie in the direction nobody re-checks by hand.

name: claude-md-lint-scope-drops-high-risk
why: this list decides which modules owe a per-module CLAUDE.md. Narrowing it silently drops high-risk modules out of scope, and the lint then reports a clean run over a smaller set than anyone agreed to.
